proposals.expected_failure_mode: If true admissions lag differs from 2 weeks (or varies over the season), peak timing may shift (phase error), producing split-to-split sensitivity despite good overall shape.
proposals.rationale: Center on the apparent lag sweet spot (2 weeks) within the best-performing family (fractional SEIRS + delayed_I). This isolates whether remaining error is primarily phase alignment vs other structural issues, while aiming for improved rolling robustness relative to more extreme delays.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May systematically lead the observed peak (too-early incidence proxy), causing early peak predictions and degraded rolling stability if the true lag is closer to 2–3 weeks.
proposals.rationale: A minimal one-step perturbation around the 2-week center to probe delay brittleness without changing structure or fractional memory. Useful to diagnose whether the series prefers a shorter clinical/reporting lag in some splits.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If 3 weeks is too long, forecasts may lag the peak and over-extend the tail, with phase error dominating and sensitivity across rolling splits.
proposals.rationale: Retain the previous best spec as an anchor comparator to assess whether improvements come from shifting delay toward 2 weeks or from other factors. Keeps all else fixed to isolate delay effects.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H compartment may be weakly identifiable in a short, peaky series, leading to unstable parameter tradeoffs (e.g., E/I/H timing) and higher rolling variability even if point fit is competitive.
proposals.rationale: Comparator focused on explicit hospitalization dynamics with direct H observation, as requested. This tests whether remaining error is better addressed by adding an H compartment (shape/translation from infections to admissions) rather than tuning delay in delayed_I.
